description: Versilia's highest-ranked table sits inside the Grand Hotel Principe di Piemonte in Viareggio, a realistic destination dinner from Forte dei Marmi. Chef Giuseppe Mancino's cuisine treats the Tuscan coast through a polished haute-cuisine lens, with tasting menus, sea-facing elegance and hotel-level service. It earns inclusion as the two-star anchor for the wider Forte dei Marmi luxury dining catchment.
highlights: Two-star Michelin destination in a grand seafront hotel, with refined Italian tasting menus and polished service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Grand Hotel Principe di Piemonte; 50 Top Italy; La Liste context

description: Lorenzo is Forte dei Marmi's classic luxury seafood institution, an address that still defines the town's old-school gastronomic identity. The dining room is elegant rather than theatrical, with precise fish cooking, important raw materials and a deep wine culture. It remains the first name many concierges and regulars mention for a serious Forte dinner.
highlights: Historic Michelin-starred seafood institution with polished service, luxury regulars and a major wine list.
sources: Michelin Guide; VisitForte; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Restaurants for Kings

description: Lux Lucis is the panoramic fine-dining restaurant at Principe Forte dei Marmi, giving the resort a glamorous rooftop counterpart to its classic seafood rooms. The cooking is contemporary, visual and technically polished, with a setting that turns sunset, the sea and the Apuan Alps into part of the experience. It is one of the strongest special-occasion tables in Forte itself.
highlights: Michelin-starred rooftop fine dining at Principe Forte dei Marmi, with sea and Apuan Alps atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; Principe Forte dei Marmi; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Tripadvisor Michelin note

description: La Magnolia is Hotel Byron's garden-framed fine-dining room, a polished Forte address with the feel of a discreet Riviera villa. The restaurant balances contemporary technique with Tuscan and coastal produce, and its chef's table gives regulars a more intimate version of the experience. It is a key Michelin-starred choice for guests who want hotel luxury without flash.
highlights: Michelin-starred Hotel Byron restaurant with garden elegance, contemporary technique and intimate chef's table appeal.
sources: Michelin Guide; Hotel Byron; VisitForte; Firenze Made in Tuscany

description: Bistrot is the fine-dining flagship of the Vaiani family group, a polished seafront-adjacent room that has helped modernize Forte's restaurant scene. The kitchen works with seafood, vegetables and local luxury ingredients in a precise but approachable style. For many affluent regulars, it offers a slightly more relaxed route into Michelin-level Forte dining.
highlights: Michelin-starred Vaiani family flagship with refined seafood cooking and polished resort service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gambero Rosso; VisitForte; Restaurants for Kings

description: Sciabola brings a younger, design-conscious fine-dining voice to Forte from inside the St. Mauritius hotel. Chef Alessandro Ferrarini's menus move between seafood and land-based ideas, with a polished tasting-menu structure and a calm hotel setting. Its recent Michelin recognition makes it one of the most important additions to the town's high-end dining map.
highlights: New-generation Michelin-starred hotel restaurant with balanced tasting menus and a refined resort setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Forte Magazine; VisitForte; Tripadvisor Michelin note

description: Romano is Viareggio's great seafood classic and a serious reason to leave Forte for dinner. The restaurant has long combined formal service, an important wine culture and precise fish cooking, while still feeling rooted in Versilia rather than generic luxury. Its longevity and Michelin status make it an essential catchment inclusion.
highlights: One-star Viareggio seafood institution, known for polished service, wine and classic Versilia fish cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tripadvisor Michelin note; La Nazione; Versilia dining guides

description: Lunasia gives Viareggio another luxury-hotel Michelin option within Forte's realistic dinner orbit. Chef Luca Landi's cooking is creative and seafood-driven, supported by attentive service and the refined context of the Plaza e de Russie. It suits diners looking for a more contemporary Versilia tasting-menu experience.
highlights: One-star hotel fine dining in Viareggio with creative seafood menus and a refined Relais and Chateaux context.
sources: Michelin Guide; Lunasia official website; Relais and Chateaux; En Primeur Club

description: Filippo is a chef-driven Pietrasanta destination that feels naturally connected to the Forte dining circuit. The format is personal and ingredient-led, with a surprise-menu spirit that gives it more gastronomic ambition than a simple Tuscan trattoria. It is a strong non-starred alternative for guests who want character and craft rather than resort gloss.
highlights: Chef-driven Pietrasanta restaurant with an ingredient-led surprise-menu approach and serious local reputation.
sources: Michelin Guide; Filippo official website; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Versilia local guides

description: Il Parco is the elegant garden restaurant of Villa Grey, offering a refined hotel-dining alternative close to the beach. The setting is discreet and romantic, with cuisine that leans into haute Tuscan and coastal references rather than scene-first resort dining. It earns a fine-dining slot for its service level, setting and clear special-occasion intent, even without a current Directus award value.
highlights: Refined Villa Grey garden restaurant with hotel polish, coastal produce and a romantic special-occasion mood.
sources: Villa Grey; Firenze Made in Tuscany; local luxury dining guides

description: Vesta brings a Milan-style luxury seafood language to the Versilia coast, with a polished room, fashion-conscious clientele and a strong seafood identity. The Marina di Pietrasanta location sits inside the same glamorous beach corridor that Forte regulars use throughout summer. It works as a high-end social dinner choice rather than a formal tasting-menu restaurant.
highlights: Fashionable seafood restaurant in the Twiga coastal orbit, combining luxury service with a strong resort scene.
sources: Michelin Guide; Vesta official website; Versilia local guides

description: Alex is a polished Marina di Pietrasanta restaurant with a cosmopolitan tone, a serious wine-cellar identity and seafood-led contemporary cooking. It sits close enough to Forte to be part of the same affluent evening circuit, especially for diners seeking something less hotel-driven. The atmosphere is refined but not stiff, making it a credible alternative to formal Michelin dining.
highlights: Michelin-selected Marina di Pietrasanta restaurant with contemporary seafood, wine focus and cosmopolitan resort mood.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tripadvisor; Versilia local guides

description: La Martinatica is one of Pietrasanta's most established serious restaurants, set in an elegant converted-mill atmosphere. The kitchen balances fish, meat and Tuscan references with enough polish to appeal to Forte diners who want a grounded but high-quality evening. It is more mature and culinary than many resort-scene alternatives.
highlights: Elegant Pietrasanta restaurant in an old-mill setting, known for polished local cooking and grown-up atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; La Martinatica official website; Versilia local guides

description: Enoteca Marcucci is the essential wine-led Pietrasanta address for serious drinkers staying in Forte. Its cellar depth, generous Tuscan cooking and late-evening social energy make it a natural alternative to a white-tablecloth seaside dinner. It is especially relevant for affluent diners who care as much about the bottle as the kitchen.
highlights: Pietrasanta wine institution with thousands of labels, generous Tuscan cooking and a sophisticated local crowd.
sources: Enoteca Marcucci official website; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Versilia local guides

description: Osteria del Mare is a high-performing Vaiani group restaurant that channels Forte's seafood culture in a more relaxed but still affluent format. The room is central, the product focus is strong and the tone suits guests who want a polished coastal dinner without committing to a tasting menu. It clears the instead-of-Michelin test as a credible night-off choice for luxury travelers.
highlights: Central upscale seafood osteria from the Vaiani group, with strong product focus and resort-polished service.
sources: Osteria del Mare official website; Gambero Rosso; Firenze Made in Tuscany; local dining guides

description: The Fratellini's is a lively, design-conscious Vaiani group address with a fashionable Forte audience and a more international rhythm. It is not trying to be formal fine dining, but it offers the setting, spend and polished dinner energy that luxury guests often want after a beach day. The menu and atmosphere make it one of the stronger social high-end options in town.
highlights: Fashionable central dining room from the Vaiani group, with modern resort energy and an affluent dinner crowd.
sources: Gambero Rosso; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Bearleaders; The Fratellini's official website

description: Aria Steak House fills the premium meat-and-grill archetype in a town otherwise dominated by seafood and beach dining. The room is grown-up, the spend profile is firmly affluent and the kitchen focuses on selected cuts rather than casual grill-house volume. It is useful for Forte regulars looking for a polished alternative to another fish dinner.
highlights: Premium steakhouse and grill option with an affluent resort crowd and a serious meat-led offer.
sources: Gambero Rosso; Aria Steak House official website; local dining guides

description: Momoyama brings a long-running Italian Japanese-fusion name into Forte's luxury resort circuit. The new Forte address is positioned as refined, convivial and close to the seafront, giving the town a polished Asian option for guests who want a break from Tuscan seafood. It is most relevant as a high-end social dinner rather than a formal tasting-menu room.
highlights: Refined Asian-fusion restaurant near the seafront, with a fashionable resort setting and serious dinner format.
sources: Momoyama official website; La Nazione; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Tripadvisor

description: D'Oria is a polished contemporary restaurant overlooking Piazza Marconi, giving Forte a central, design-conscious alternative to its hotel and beachfront rooms. The menu is curated by Michelin-starred chef Giuseppe Molaro and is built around a clean, modern interpretation of Versilia ingredients. It fits the affluent dinner set because of its location, chef signature and refined contemporary style.
highlights: Contemporary Piazza Marconi restaurant with a chef-signed menu and elegant central Forte atmosphere.
sources: D'Oria official website; Firenze Made in Tuscany; local dining guides

description: La Cucina del Giardino is a relaxed but polished Forte restaurant built around fresh fish, local produce and a garden mood. It does not compete on formality, yet it attracts the kind of guests who want a softer evening without dropping into casual tourist dining. The appeal is local, seasonal and adult rather than scene-led.
highlights: Garden-side Forte restaurant with fresh fish, local ingredients and a relaxed but affluent dinner profile.
sources: La Cucina del Giardino official website; Tripadvisor; local Forte dining guides

description: Alpemare is one of Forte dei Marmi's defining luxury beach-club restaurants, combining beach service, events and a gourmet seaside restaurant. The experience is polished, high-spend and unmistakably resort-driven, with the kind of service and setting expected by affluent Versilia regulars. It is a core beach-club inclusion rather than a generic waterfront restaurant.
highlights: Luxury beach club with gourmet restaurant, seaside service and a polished Versilia resort atmosphere.
sources: Alpemare official website; OpenTable; Firenze Made in Tuscany; beach-club guides

description: Maito is a historic Forte beach restaurant and club whose reputation rests on seafood, coastal glamour and more than six decades of resort continuity. It has the adult, old-money beach energy that defines Forte rather than a pure party-club identity. For lunch, sunset or dinner by the sand, it remains one of the town's essential beach-club tables.
highlights: Historic beach restaurant and club with seafood, polished service and old-school Forte glamour.
sources: Maito official website; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Bearleaders; local beach-club guides

description: Gilda is both a beach club and a serious seasonal seaside restaurant, set directly on the Tyrrhenian shore. The tone is elegant and resort-social, with private beach service, gazebos and a seafood-focused restaurant offer. It belongs in the beach-club category because the dining experience is inseparable from the club's beach hospitality.
highlights: Seasonal beach club and restaurant with private gazebos, seafood and a polished Forte seaside atmosphere.
sources: Gilda official website; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Gambero Rosso; beach-club guides

description: Bambaissa is the restaurant of Augustus Beach Club, one of Forte's most established luxury-hotel beach addresses. The atmosphere is refined and romantic, with beach-club service, seaside dining and the upscale hospitality context of the Augustus world. It is most compelling for guests who want a complete resort beach experience with a serious dinner or long lunch.
highlights: Augustus Beach Club restaurant with refined seaside dining, hotel-level hospitality and luxury resort atmosphere.
sources: Augustus Beach Club; Bearleaders; Firenze Made in Tuscany; beach-club guides

description: Dalmazia is the beach restaurant connected to Principe Forte dei Marmi, giving the hotel a more relaxed but still luxury seaside expression. The setting uses verandas, cabanas and beach-club service, while the kitchen is positioned around regional produce and coastal flavors. It is a true beach-club dining venue rather than simply a restaurant with a view.
highlights: Principe Forte dei Marmi beach restaurant with cabanas, verandas and refined Tuscan coastal cooking.
sources: Principe Forte dei Marmi; La Esplora; Firenze Made in Tuscany; beach-club guides

restaurant_name: Roberto Forte dei Marmi - Il Baretto Mare
description: Roberto Forte dei Marmi brings the Il Baretto al Mare spirit to a beachfront club setting, combining Milanese social polish with Versilia beach culture. The venue is especially relevant in 2026 because the Bagni Roberto site has been repositioned within the luxury fashion-hospitality conversation. It is best understood as a high-end beach-club restaurant for a stylish, international crowd.
highlights: Fashion-linked beachfront dining and club address with Il Baretto al Mare heritage and Milanese resort energy.
sources: Roberto Forte dei Marmi official website; Vogue; local luxury travel coverage

description: Twiga is the area's most recognizable high-energy luxury beach club, sitting just down the coast in Marina di Pietrasanta but still inside the Forte resort orbit. Dining here is wrapped into a broader day-to-night club experience, so it suits guests who want glamour, music and seaside scene alongside a polished restaurant offer. It is included as a beach club, not as a quiet gastronomic restaurant.
highlights: Iconic Versilia beach club with refined beach service, dining and a more glamorous day-to-night scene.
sources: Twiga official website; Michelin Guide; local beach-club guides

description: Bagno Annetta is a classic Forte beach-club restaurant with a sea-view veranda and a strong fresh-fish identity. The appeal is not theatrical luxury but refined continuity, beach service and a loyal affluent summer clientele. It offers exactly the kind of old-Forte seaside meal that sophisticated regulars value.
highlights: Traditional beach club with sea-view veranda, fresh fish and a loyal Forte summer clientele.
sources: Bagno Annetta official website; beach-club guides; local Forte recommendations

description: Bagno Piero is one of Forte's most elegant historic beach clubs, known for its long tradition and understated luxury. Its restaurant and beach service appeal to a quieter, more established audience than the louder club names. The venue represents the old-school Versilia beach-club archetype with enough polish to matter to affluent diners.
highlights: Historic 1930s beach club with understated luxury, beach service and a refined regulars' atmosphere.
sources: Bagno Piero official website; local beach-club guides; Vogue context

description: Bagno Camilla is a beach-club restaurant for diners who want the Forte seaside ritual in a calmer and more culinary register. The setting is elegant, sea-facing and explicitly built around a restaurant offer rather than just sunbeds and drinks. It is especially useful as a lower-key but still affluent alternative to the headline beach clubs.
highlights: Elegant sea-view beach club restaurant with creative coastal cooking and a quieter affluent profile.
sources: Bagno Camilla official website; Firenze Made in Tuscany; local beach-club guides

description: Pesce Baracca is the protected local-favorite pick for diners who want Forte's seafood culture in a livelier, less formal frame. The concept combines fish-market freshness with a restaurant format and a central resort location, making it relaxed without feeling disposable. It is ideal for a casual but still quality-conscious dinner after several starred meals.
highlights: Beloved central seafood-market restaurant with fresh local catch, relaxed energy and strong local credibility.
sources: Pesce Baracca official website; Gambero Rosso; Bearleaders; local Forte recommendations

description: Bagno Silvio is one of Forte's most meaningful relaxed local classics, with more than a century of family beach and restaurant history. The appeal is not luxury staging, but continuity, seafood, sand-underfoot atmosphere and the feeling of an address regulars genuinely protect. It fits the informal local favorite role because it gives affluent visitors a culturally specific Forte meal without pretending to be fine dining.
highlights: Century-old family beach restaurant with seafood, local continuity and a beloved old-Forte atmosphere.
sources: Firenze Made in Tuscany; Bagni del Forte; local Forte recommendations

description: Pozzo di Bugia in Querceta gives Forte diners a relaxed inland counterpoint to beach seafood and hotel gastronomy. The cooking is hearty, Tuscan and grill-friendly, with a cellar-led trattoria spirit that sophisticated locals continue to recommend. It is included as an informal favorite because it feels rooted, adult and proper for dinner.
highlights: Querceta trattoria and wine-led local favorite with Tuscan cooking, grill appeal and relaxed dinner credibility.
sources: Pozzo di Bugia official website; Nina Nasre local recommendations; Versilia local guides

description: Il Fortino is a central Forte seafood restaurant on Piazza del Fortino, useful for a relaxed local-style dinner in the heart of town. The veranda, seafood focus and classic resort positioning make it more relevant than casual convenience dining. It works best for guests who want a straightforward Forte institution between more ambitious reservations.
highlights: Central seafood restaurant with veranda seating, town-square energy and a relaxed local-institution role.
sources: Il Fortino official website; Tripadvisor; local Forte dining guides

description: Bagno Santa Maria is a polished but relaxed local beach restaurant that keeps Forte's traditional seaside rhythm intact. The restaurant leans into Versilian dishes, fish and wine rather than spectacle, making it a good informal counterweight to the louder luxury clubs. It is included as a local favorite because the experience feels distinctly Forte while remaining suitable for sophisticated travelers.
highlights: Refined local beach restaurant with Versilian dishes, seafood and a quieter old-Forte seaside atmosphere.
sources: Bagno Santa Maria official website; Firenze Made in Tuscany; Bagni del Forte; local beach-club guides
